# Agent web UI

The admin service's browser-facing surfaces for chatting with agents: the admin chat UI, Web Push, the PWA shell and dev auto-login. The pages are server-rendered HTML from `admin/src/admin-ui.ts` (routes) and `admin/src/admin-ui-pages.ts` (rendering); see [admin-service.md](./admin-service.md#admin-ui) for the module map and [agent.md](./agent.md) for the platform architecture. Auth modes and bearer scopes for the JSON API are in [agent-api.md](./agent-api.md).

Other admin pages (agent list, create form and detail, `/admin/account`, `/admin/accounts`) are described in [admin-service.md](./admin-service.md) and [self-serve.md](./self-serve.md). Pages for coding-specific features (tasks, sessions and the public task board) belong to the [shipwright repository](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/agent-web-ui.md) and arrive through admin extensions.

---

## Admin chat UI (`admin-ui.ts`, `admin-ui-pages.ts`, `http-chat-client.ts`)

Mounted at `/admin/chat*`. Requires a session cookie or bearer token (the same auth as the rest of the admin UI). Admins see every agent. Other users see and use only agents they may access (agent members, and account members when self-serve is on); every route checks access, and thread-scoped routes also verify that the thread belongs to the agent in the URL (`403` otherwise). When the chat client is configured, the pages show a thread browser, thread detail and message creation. When it is absent, every route renders in degraded mode.

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/chat` | List threads for a selected agent. Query params: `agentId` (optional, pre-selects an agent in the dropdown) and `q` (optional, filters threads by title substring). Renders the agent selector, search box and thread list; with no agent selected it shows an empty-state prompt. `403` when a non-admin selects an agent they cannot access. Returns `text/html`. |
| GET | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId` | View one thread. See "Thread page" below. Returns `text/html`. |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads` | Create a thread. Body: form-encoded `title` (optional). Redirects to the new thread (302); on a chat-service error redirects back to the agent's thread list (302). |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId/rename` | Rename a thread. Body: form-encoded `title`. A blank title is a no-op. Always redirects back to the thread (302). |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId/delete` | Delete a thread, then redirect to the agent's thread list (302). Errors are swallowed; there is no error banner. |
| GET | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId/messages.json` | JSON poll endpoint. Supports `?since=<messageId>`. Returns `{ messages }` where each entry carries an explicit field set (`id`, `role`, `createdAt`, `repliedAt`, `progressPhase`, `progressSeq`) plus a server-rendered `bubbleHtml`, so a polled bubble is byte-identical to one from a full reload. Returns `{ messages: [] }` when the chat service is absent or errors. |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId/messages.json` | JSON send. Body: `{ "body": string }`. Returns `{ message }`; `400` for an empty or malformed body, `500` on failure. |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId/messages/upload` | JSON send with an optional file (the route the thread page's send box uses). Body: `multipart/form-data` with `body` (optional) and `file` (optional); at least one is required. Returns `{ message }` (201), or `{ error }` with 400 (missing body and file), 413 (attachment over 10 MB), 415 (disallowed type), 503 (chat service not configured). |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId/messages` | Form-post send with the same fields plus `role` (`user` or `assistant`, default `user`). Redirects back to the thread whether or not it succeeds. Legacy; the `/upload` route is preferred. |
| GET | `/admin/chat/:agentId/threads/:threadId/messages/:messageId/attachment` | Attachment proxy. The browser never holds the chat service's admin token, so this route fetches the bytes with `chatClient.getAttachment()` and re-serves them with `Content-Disposition: inline`. Audio attachments get a real `audio/*` `Content-Type` derived from the filename extension (`audioContentTypeForFilename` in `attachment-validation.ts`: `.wav`, `.mp3`, `.webm`, `.ogg`, `.m4a`) so they play inline in `<audio>`; anything else is `application/octet-stream`. `404` when there is no attachment, `503` when the chat service is not configured. |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/push/subscribe`, `/admin/chat/:agentId/push/unsubscribe` | Web Push subscription management for the calling user. See "Web Push". |

Send routes (`/messages`, `/messages.json`, `/messages/upload`) return `403` when the agent's account is suspended or its trial has expired; read-only history stays available, and platform admins and agents without an account are exempt.

### Thread page

- **Header.** Thread title, plus aggregated token and cost stats (`<input> in / <output> out | $<cost>`) when the chat service has usage for the thread. Rename and delete controls, and the push toggle when push is enabled.
- **Messages.** Role-labelled bubbles. Assistant messages are markdown-rendered (HTML is escaped first, then markdown patterns are applied by `renderMarkdown()`), with response markers parsed out of the text by `chat-markers.ts` (an `[upload:...]` path becomes an artifact badge and a `[plan:url]` becomes a link badge; `[silent]`, `[speak:...]` and `[react:...]` are stripped). Assistant messages with usage data show a per-message `<in> in / <out> out · $<cost>` badge.
- **Errors and retry.** A reply with `errorKind` set shows an error badge. For `cancelled`, `incomplete` and `stalled` errors it also shows a Retry button that resends the text of the preceding user message.
- **Live status bubble.** While the last user message is unreplied, the page renders a bubble with the stable DOM id `live-status-bubble`. A client-side one-second ticker shows elapsed time with no network dependency, so the UI never goes silent. A milestone label from the message's `progressPhase` (mapped through `PROGRESS_LABELS` in `@app-vitals/agent-lib/progress-phases`) refreshes from the `messages.json` poll, which runs every 2 s while a reply is pending and every 10 s when idle. If `progressSeq` has not advanced for `STALL_WARN_AFTER_MS` (2 minutes) the bubble gets the `chat-stall-indicator` warning style; `ABSOLUTE_MAX_MS` (65 minutes, matching the chat claim TTL) is the hard stop.
- **Attachments.** Audio attachments (microphone recordings and TTS replies) render from the attachment proxy (user recordings as a native `<audio controls>`; assistant voice replies as the control described below); the choice is made by filename extension (`isAudioFilename`) inside the shared `renderChatMessageBubble()`, so a live poll and a reload render the same. Other attachments render as a filename badge. Uploads are limited to 10 MB (`MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`) and to images, PDF, JSON, `text/*` and audio types (`attachment-validation.ts`). A mic button (`#mic-btn`) records with `MediaRecorder`/`getUserMedia` and posts the blob through the `/upload` route; it hides itself where those APIs are missing.
- **Voice reply control.** Assistant audio replies replace the tiny native player with a 56px round `<button>` (`aria-label` toggles Play/Pause), elapsed/total time and a thin progress bar, driven by a hidden `<audio>` element. One delegated, capture-phase script handles click and the `timeupdate`/`loadedmetadata`/`ended` events, so bubbles inserted by polling work with no per-node wiring; starting one reply pauses any other. The transcript above is unchanged. If the audio element fires `error`, the control is replaced by "Could not play this reply" and a direct download link. The attachment proxy honours a single `Range` (`bytes=a-b`, `bytes=a-`, `bytes=-n`): 206 with `Content-Range`, 416 with `Content-Range: bytes */total` when unsatisfiable, and 200 with `Accept-Ranges: bytes` and `Content-Length` otherwise (iOS Safari requires byte ranges for media). Parsing lives in `admin/src/http-range.ts`.
- **Thread sidebar.** Lists all of the agent's threads. At 640px and below it becomes a CSS-only off-canvas drawer (hamburger toggle, scrim, Escape to close), and the stats and rename/delete controls move out of the collapsed header.

### Degraded mode and configuration

When no chat client is configured, every chat route still returns `200`, rendering a notice that names the two variables below instead of a thread list or messages (the JSON routes return empty results or `503`).

- `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL`: base URL of the chat service (for example `http://chat:3000`).
- `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_ADMIN_TOKEN`: bearer token for admin-side chat service access. Both must be set for the admin UI to reach threads and messages.

## Web Push

Push notifications tell a user that an agent has replied in a thread they are watching. Sending a user message records that user as a watcher of the thread (`PushService.recordWatch`) when push is enabled; push is enabled only when `PushService` exists and a VAPID public key is configured. Module details are in [admin-service.md](./admin-service.md#web-push).

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/push/subscribe` | session or bearer | Store a browser push subscription for the calling user. Body: `{ endpoint, p256dh, auth }`. `400` when a field is missing, `500` if storing fails, `503` when push is disabled. |
| POST | `/admin/chat/:agentId/push/unsubscribe` | session or bearer | Remove a subscription. Body: `{ endpoint }`. Scoped to the caller, so a stale endpoint cannot prune someone else's subscription. |
| POST | `/admin/push/notify` | bearer token (`SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`) | Webhook the chat service calls when an agent posts a reply. Body: `{ threadId, agentId, title?, preview? }`. Returns `{ ok: true, delivered, pruned }`, where `pruned` counts subscriptions removed after the push provider reported them gone (404/410). `503` when push is disabled or the webhook token is unset, `401` when the bearer token is missing or wrong, `400` for a malformed body. |

The thread page includes the push toggle (`push-toggle.ts`) only when push is enabled. The browser permission prompt appears only when the user clicks the toggle, never on load; a previously denied permission shows static guidance, and iOS Safari outside an installed PWA shows "Add to Home Screen" guidance.

What a notification reveals on a lock screen is governed by `push-content.ts`: three levels (`generic`, `title`, `preview`), capped by the operator ceiling `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_MAX_DETAIL` (default `title`) and by each subscription's opt-in (default `generic`). Agent names, ids, repo names, file paths and costs never appear in visible fields, and user-authored text is scrubbed for those shapes.

`admin/src/admin-ui-push-test.ts` defines a `POST /admin/push/test` route (admin-only, sends a fixed test notification to the caller's own subscriptions, `503` when push is disabled) and a "Send test notification" button fragment. The platform admin app does not mount either itself: `registerPushTestRoute` is called from no module in this repository, so an extension or a settings page that wants the control has to register it.

**Configuration:**

- Web Push requires all three of `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` and `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_VAPID_SUBJECT`. With any missing, the routes degrade (`503`) and the thread page renders no toggle.
- `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`: the shared bearer token the chat service presents to `/admin/push/notify`.
- `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_PUSH_MAX_DETAIL` (optional): the operator ceiling described above.
- See [admin-service.md](./admin-service.md#configuration) for the grouped list and [configuration-agent.md](./configuration-agent.md) for the full reference.

## Dev auto-login (`admin-ui.ts`)

`GET /admin/dev-login` is a local convenience and **deny by default**. The route returns `404` unless `devAuthEnabled=true` is injected into `createAdminUIApp()`. That flag comes from `isDevAuthAllowed()` in `dev-auth-guard.ts`, which requires `ADMIN_DEV_AUTH=true` and is always false when `NODE_ENV=production`, whatever `ADMIN_DEV_AUTH` says. When enabled, it mints an `admin_session` JWT cookie (user id `dev`, email `dev@localhost`, admin) and redirects to `/admin/agents`, with no Google or Okta login.

## PWA shell

The admin console is an installable Progressive Web App. Authenticated `/admin/*` pages include a manifest link and service-worker registration in their `<head>` through `renderPwaHeadTags()` (`admin/src/pwa.ts`), but only when `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_APP_BASE_URL` starts with `https://`; on plain HTTP the tags are omitted and the rest of the admin UI works unchanged. The manifest scope is always `/admin/`. The start URL defaults to `/admin/chat`; the head script rewrites the manifest link to `?start=<current pathname>` so "Add to Home Screen" launches back into the page the user was on. `sanitizeStartUrl()` accepts only in-scope `/admin/...` paths and falls back to the default for anything else (external or protocol-relative URLs, traversal, encoded variants, asset and auth routes such as `/admin/icons/*`, `/admin/logout` and OAuth callbacks).

Caching is deliberately austere. Only the offline fallback page and the six icons are precached; no HTML documents, JSON routes or authenticated content are ever cached, because a cached page on a shared or stolen phone would be a data leak. `getPrecacheList()` and `shouldCachePwaRequest()` are that security boundary.

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/manifest.webmanifest` | none | Web app manifest (`application/manifest+json`). Unauthenticated, because browsers fetch it with `credentials: omit`. Accepts `?start=` as above. Contains the app name, icons, scope `/admin/`, start URL, theme and background colours from `admin/src/theme-tokens.json`, and `display: standalone`. |
| GET | `/admin/sw.js` | none | Service worker script from `buildServiceWorkerBody()`, served with `Cache-Control: no-cache` so version bumps take effect. The cache name embeds the app version. It handles `install`, `activate`, `fetch`, `push` and `notificationclick`: `fetch` serves cached responses only for GET requests to precached URLs, `push` shows a notification from a JSON payload (`title`, `body`, `url`, optional `tag`, which defaults to `shipwright-agent-reply`), and `notificationclick` focuses or opens the target URL. |
| GET | `/admin/offline.html` | none | Self-contained offline fallback page with inline CSS and no external resources. |
| GET | `/admin/icons/:filename` | none | PWA icon PNG with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400`. Allowed names are the `PWA_ICONS` set: `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `icon-maskable-192.png`, `icon-maskable-512.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png` (180x180) and `favicon-32.png`. Unknown names return `404`. Files are the committed PNGs in `admin/pwa-assets/icons/`. |

## Chatting with an agent

The agent has no HTTP chat endpoint. Chat flows through the chat service: the admin console's chat pages post user messages to it, and the agent's chat poll loop (`runtime/chat-poller.ts`) claims them, runs them through Claude and posts the replies. See [agent-runtime.md](./agent-runtime.md#entry-points-that-call-claude) for the runtime side.
